# 1 Enoch Chapter 55 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 55:3 — cognate figure: 'troubled with great trouble' vs. 'disturbed with great disturbance' vs. 'shaken with violent agitation'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "were-troubled with-great-trouble" | Preserves Ge'ez cognate figure (same root for verb and noun) |
| LOGOS | "were disturbed with great disturbance" | Same cognate figure, slightly more modern |
| PNEUMA | "were shaken with violent agitation" | Dynamic; loses the cognate figure |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted 'were troubled with great trouble' (EMET). The Ge'ez cognate figure is significant as a literary intensifier and should be preserved. PNEUMA's 'violent agitation' is vivid but loses the echo.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET. Literary structure preserved.

---

## 55:7 — Michael's address: 'Wherefore art thou disquieted' vs. 'Why are you so troubled' vs. 'Why has this vision shaken you'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Wherefore art-thou disquieted with such a vision" | Archaic second person singular; literal |
| LOGOS | "Why are you so troubled by this vision" | Modern formal; clear |
| PNEUMA | "Why has this vision shaken you so completely" | Adds 'completely'; shifts agency to the vision |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. Michael's speech should be direct and clear. EMET's archaic form creates unnecessary distance; PNEUMA's expansion adds an element not present in the Ge'ez.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 55:8 — 'inquisition' vs. 'investigation and exposure' for the fate of sinners

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "an-inquisition" | Traditional rendering; forensic Ge'ez term |
| LOGOS | "an inquisition" | Agrees — judicial examination |
| PNEUMA | "full inquisition" / "investigation and exposure" | Minor expansion for clarity |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained 'an inquisition' (EMET/LOGOS). The compact term preserves the forensic register. All three translators ultimately converge on the core term.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---
